front.title: Dynamic Authorization Protocol (DAP): Out-of-Band Visual Transaction Authorization for Untrusted Terminals

abstract.t: This document specifies the Dynamic Authorization Protocol (DAP), an Out-of-Band (OOB) visual transaction authorization protocol, used as a second factor, for electronic financial transactions initiated on untrusted terminals. The terminal displays a cryptographically protected challenge as a Quick Response (QR) code. A trusted mobile device of the user, which needs no network connection, scans the code, verifies it with HMAC-SHA-256, shows the transaction details for confirmation ("What You See Is What You Sign"), and then reveals a one-time authorizer code protected with AES-256. Each challenge is bound to one transaction and expires within 120 seconds. The document also describes the provisioning of the shared key through a dual-channel XOR split-key exchange, its activation, and the templates used to display transactions. DAP targets Man-in-the- Middle (MITM) and Man-in-the-Browser (MITB) adversaries that control the terminal and alter transaction parameters.
